title: range-slot-packer: kernel-fit slot packing with KV prefill and continuous-batching hook
author: Maya Patel
description: Add a new range-slot-packer scheduler that groups inflight requests by sequence-length ranges and chooses slot sizes based on a kernel-fit scoring function; integrates a KV-prefill warmup path for large-cohort requests and exposes a continuous-batching hook so the runtime can merge near-term pending requests within a short window. Motivation: mixed-seqlen production traffic drives excessive padding and suboptimal kernel utilization. This PR implements a compact heuristic that minimizes padded tokens while preferring kernels that have better memory-lane alignment for the given slot, and it also addresses cold-KV stalls by issuing an opportunistic prefill for cohorts likely to miss cache. Design highlights: 1) Seqlen ranges are configurable (default ranges: 1-32, 33-128, 129-512) and the slot-packer tries power-of-two-aligned lengths within ranges to improve kernel-fit. 2) Kernel-fit scoring: score = pad_token_cost * padded_tokens + kernel_latency_penalty * expected_kernel_mismatch + kv_warmup_penalty * missing_kv_probability. Scores are computed from lightweight telemetry histograms and a small static table per architecture. 3) KV prefill: when a cohort has a significant fraction of requests with past KV miss probability > 0.15, the scheduler issues a batched KV prefill that overlaps with the initial batch dispatch to amortize the first-token stall. Prefill is lightweight and opt-in per model via config. 4) Continuous-batching hook: scheduler will hold merging window up to 60ms (configurable) and will opportunistically merge small pending batches across adjacent ranges when score savings exceed a threshold. 5) Metrics/telemetry: adds pad_tokens_saved, kernel_fit_score, kv_prefill_count, continuous_merge_count and per-route pad_ratio. 6) Safety: conservative fallbacks for latency-sensitive routes (route config flag), and disabled prefill on low-memory devices. Implementation notes: new scheduler module runtime/batching/range_slot_packer.{cpp,h} implements the heuristic and integrates with existing BatchComposer interface; serving/kernel_selector adapted to expose kernel affinity estimates; serving/kv_cache/prefill implements batched prefill path and the KV warmup state machine; small additions to the continuous-batcher to accept cross-range merges. Includes unit tests, microbench harness, and an end-to-end perf test using the lab fixture. Benchmarks: internal lm-mix workload (40% short, 40% mid, 20% long) on an a100-40g cluster: median response latency -14%, p95 -8%, p99 -9%; token-cost per request decreased 21% vs current seqlen-strict bucketer for the same quality target. The PR is intentionally conservative in default config but provides knobs for teams to tune.

review_comments: Rafael Gomez: Nice direction. Please add a rationale for the default ranges and a short note on why we choose power-of-two alignment. Also add a unit test for the kernel-affinity table stub.
Maya Patel: Added rationale in docs and a new unit test covering kernel_affinity_table fallbacks (see commit b4c9a2d).
Anita Singh: KV prefill looks promising but I'm worried about memory pressure on smaller instances. Can we gate prefill behind available_kv_memory check?
Maya Patel: Prefill now checks device_kv_budget and disables on devices that report < 128MB spare KV budget (commit f1a9b22).
Jordan Lee: CI perf run initially showed a flaky p99 regression in the continuous merge path. Found a race in the merge timer; suggested using a compare-and-swap to guard state transitions.
Maya Patel: Race fixed with CAS and added flakeguard in CI; re-ran perf suites and numbers stabilized (commit f7c2d33).
Anita Singh: Approving after the prefill budget guard and telemetry additions.
release_notes: Introduce range-slot-packer: a configurable seqlen-range batching heuristic that reduces padding and improves kernel utilization. Adds optional KV prefill warmup and new telemetry for pad savings. Default config is conservative.
